scope: Corollary 1.3 (Exact convolution and polynomial multiplication) of the manuscript “An explicit power saving for the exact discrete Fourier transform” (preprints/An-explicit-power-saving-for-the-exact-discrete-Fourier-transform-September-25-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 130 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 670d0115ea2553e6), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 3. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is a single deterministic algorithm which, for every positive integer n and every a, b ∈ Cn, computes the linear convolution ck = X 0≤r,s<n r+s=k arbs, 0 ≤ k ≤ 2n − 2. Equivalently, it multiplies two complex polynomials of degree less than n. In the exact complex field- operation, specified-root, and address cost model above, with general field multiplication permitted for the pointwise products, the total running time, including scalar preparation, schedule construction, padding, and index work, is O  n(log n)θ (log log n)4−θ  (n → ∞), and hence is eventually O(n(log n)1−10−13 ). This is a bilinear arithmetic algorithm, not an input- linear circuit: its pointwise products multiply a value linear in a by a value linear in b.
